dedupe_keys.name: attest t4 1 tool for ancillary services procurement in day ahead operation planning of the distribution network

description: Muhammad Usman and Baraa Mohandes at the Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology publish the ATTEST T4.1 distribution-flexibility procurement tool. It implements a sequential linearisation algorithm in Julia for stochastic, multi-period AC optimal power flow in active distribution systems. Users select a network input, an output destination and the flexible resources to include, then run the main Julia script. The October 2023 Zenodo software archive is free under EUPL 1.2. The repository links the method paper in IEEE Transactions on Power Systems. Geographic coverage, operating periods and resource assumptions depend on the selected network; the brief README does not establish a complete dependency or solver checklist. The implementation can support day-ahead procurement and flexibility-scheduling simulations. Its expected device states are inputs to the separately archived ATTEST real-time activation tool. No existing catalogue parent explicitly covers this module. The code and results were not executed.
